chapter_theme: Having release (முத்தியுடைமை): those in release have the Father's full grace, purified tattvas and a devotion in which their deeds have fallen away, and know the supreme bliss; a second, obscure verse pictures the search for the heart's fruit.

2633.reading: Those who, in release, have received the Father's full grace, reached the purification of the tattvas, and come into true devotion, in which their own service, true penance and action have left deeds behind, are knowers of the supreme bliss.
2633.nuance: தத்துவ சுத்தி (purification of the tattvas) is a Siddhanta stage in which the soul sees the constituents of its world as not itself. The syntax of line 3 is loose; வினைவிட்ட may qualify the devotion or the people. பரானந்த போதர் may also be 'those awakened to supreme bliss'.

2634.reading: When the strong-legged bird that sought rich fruit wanders seeking the fruit of the heart, the four who have gained the good light a lamp in their hand in the fire of the throat-fruit and search.
2634.nuance: The verse is symbolic and its key terms can't be fixed from the Tamil. The bird may be the soul; களங்கனி may be the dark kala fruit or the 'fruit in the throat', a yogic centre; நால்வர் may be the followers of the four paths or four sages. I give only the surface.
